key_insight: The paper compares direct and indirect PINN formulations for Dirichlet boundary control of semilinear parabolic PDEs, and provides a conditional error theory for the indirect method.
engineering_relevance: This supports more reliable neural solvers for PDE-constrained control problems where boundary actuation and state accuracy matter in simulation, optimization, and design.
method: Direct PINN: separate networks for state and control, trained on a penalized tracking objective.
Indirect PINN: jointly learns state, adjoint, and control by enforcing the first-order optimality system with soft penalties for coupling and boundary/terminal conditions.
Error analysis: decomposes total error into approximation, optimization, quadrature, and soft-constraint terms, then derives a residual-based indicator.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments on two manufactured test problems—a cubic reaction-diffusion equation and a linear test with nontrivial boundary control and adjoint—showing behavior of both formulations.
watch_item: The main reliability bounds are conditional on regularity, network approximability, soft-constraint residual control, and staying near the reference optimal solution.
paper_title: Direct and Indirect Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Dirichlet Boundary Control of Semilinear Parabolic Equations: A Conditional Error Analysis
